title: Why Seasons Change: Earth's Tilted Orbit Explained

scenes.title: Earth's Tilted Dance
scenes.narration: Seasons are not caused by Earth's distance from the Sun, but by its axial tilt of 23.5 degrees. This constant tilt, as Earth orbits, dramatically changes how much direct sunlight different regions receive.

scenes.title: Direct vs. Indirect Sunlight
scenes.narration: When a hemisphere tilts towards the Sun, it gets more direct, concentrated sunlight, leading to summer. Conversely, tilting away means indirect, spread-out sunlight, causing winter.

scenes.title: The Orbital Cycle & Constant Tilt
scenes.narration: Earth's 23.5-degree axial tilt remains constant relative to space as it orbits the Sun. This consistent orientation ensures that different hemispheres are alternately exposed to more direct solar radiation throughout the year.

scenes.title: Solstices and Equinoxes
scenes.narration: The summer solstice marks the maximum tilt towards the Sun, while the winter solstice is the maximum tilt away. The equinoxes occur when the tilt is neither towards nor away, resulting in nearly equal day and night.

scenes.title: Impact on Life & Climate
scenes.narration: This annual cycle of seasons profoundly impacts Earth's climate zones, influencing everything from agricultural patterns to animal migration. Understanding the tilt helps us predict weather and manage resources globally.
